correspondence.finding: Full selected extent supported at generalized corridor scale.
correspondence.correspondence: Full selected extent supported at generalized corridor scale.

subreaches.observation: The entire initial northward course follows a mapped stream with small continental-wetland patches, then joins the separately mapped Arroyo de Valeriano branch. The selected feeder is west of that separate branch; nearby lake labels are not borrowed.

subreaches.name: Río Valeriano / Río Conay
subreaches.observation: The selected corridor turns northwest along Valeriano, receives the Laguna Chica branch and reaches the Laguna Grande junction, then follows Conay southwest past the Corral and Albaricoque tributary settings toward Chollay.

subreaches.name: Río del Tránsito / Río Huasco
subreaches.observation: After the Chollay confluence the route follows Tránsito northwest, with Pinte, Las Pircas and El Tabaco among mapped side-channel settings. Carmen enters from the south near Alto del Carmen; downstream labels change to Huasco.

subreaches.name: Embalse Santa Juana
subreaches.observation: The model passes through the elongated artificial-wetland polygon between the mapped Huasco inlet and outlet. The primary operator identifies Santa Juana as regulating the Huasco; the government evaluation describes its controlled outlets and spillway.

subreaches.setting: Lower valley and actual coastal terminal
subreaches.name: Río Huasco
subreaches.observation: The westward lower river is continuous through the Vallenar–Freirina–Huasco Bajo corridor into the mapped fluvial/coastal wetland transition. Its terminal lies at the Pacific coastal setting, rather than an inland lake. Exact present mouth position is not asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Initial southern feeder and northward chain
correspondence.finding: The Joe Lake original shows a lake-rich headward landscape with small streams and elongate waterbodies across the selected initial feeder. No hydronym was established for the feeder itself. The source was read across the initial component; not every short selected link could be securely resolved.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward bend and upper lake connections
correspondence.finding: Original66J shows the intervening stream network, larger elongate lake and subsequent northeast/northward lake-and-stream setting of the selected eastward excursion. The small connectors and their branch choice are not elevated from broad spatial agreement to full correspondence.

The northern Joe Lake sheet covers the long northwest return through elongated waterbodies, intervening channels and rapid-marked reaches to the northern sheet edge. No name is applied to every lake passage or feeder. Some connector/junction correspondence remains unresolved.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle corridor, western river approach and sheet-boundary transition
correspondence.finding: The McLoughlin Bay original maps the incoming northwest-trending corridor and prints Simpson River on the larger western river. This is substantive original-map support for a bounded Simpson River candidate, but it does not alone establish all selected junctions or the later selected coastal branch.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower western excursion and northeast return
correspondence.finding: The selected model crosses west of the available66O map frame, continues northwest/north and then bends northeast. The regional1974 compilation labels Simpson River but does not resolve this selected lower route, material branching or return. Detailed original-map correspondence is missing.

correspondence.component_scope: Final stream and actual coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: The selected terminal is east of the named Simpson River mouth described in ARC403. The sailing directions separately note many stream mouths farther east. No read original map establishes the selected outlet, its name or its relationship to the Simpson corridor. The nearby named river mouth is not substituted for the selected terminal.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwestern opening and Rio Regina junction distinction
correspondence.finding: The original hydrographic base supplies the full small northern/eastern opening and its northeastward feeder through the Cassiporé locality. The separate southeastern Rio Regina channel and material meeting with the downstream corridor are visible. This resolves the coverage limitation of the municipal map's first headward stretch.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete bounded geographic correspondence; initial feeder hydronym left null.

correspondence.component_scope: Interior Cassiporé and Segundo Braço junction
correspondence.finding: Original maps depict the Cassiporé's northeastward corridor and the selected western branch entering from the Rio Segundo Braço. The tributary is traced as its own branch, with its complete selected lower connection.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary corridor scale; representative identity does not erase tributary distinction.
correspondence.mapped_component_name: Rio Cassiporé / Rio Segundo Braço junction

correspondence.component_scope: Vila Velha bends and northward lowland transition
correspondence.finding: The river continues northeast through the interior settlement corridor, bends near Vila Velha and then becomes predominantly northward in the Cabo Orange lowlands. The original thematic maps and hydrography prose agree with that route.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete; no unread connector between the interior map and the coastal maps.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower wetland corridor, lateral Lago Maruani and estuarine ending
correspondence.finding: The lower northward channel is distinct from the western Lago Maruani side waterbody and its short connector. The selected path stays in the river and passes Taperebá to its estuarine endpoint; the estuary continues into the Atlantic west of Cabo Cassiporé. The park maps show the associated várzea, inundated fields and mangrove/fluvio-marine coastal setting. No selected through-lake or reservoir passage is depicted.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete lower and actual terminal setting, with no exact coastline-point claim.

correspondence.finding: Selected geometry read completely for orientation; no admissible original map covering this entire fragment was acquired.
correspondence.correspondence: Selected geometry read completely for orientation; no admissible original map covering this entire fragment was acquired.
correspondence.unresolved: Headward lake/channel relationships, material inflows, the complete upper route and its actual connection to the downstream named corridor remain unobserved.
correspondence.orientation_only: The retained fragment initially runs northwest, bends south, and later turns east/southeast toward its successor. These are model observations, not source-derived hydrographic facts.

correspondence.finding: Partial downstream regional correspondence; the northern approach from the Labrador fragment is missing.
correspondence.correspondence: Partial downstream regional correspondence; the northern approach from the Labrador fragment is missing.

observations: BAPE236 Figure2 shows the Saint-Paul entering from the north, bending southeast and east, receiving the distinct Ruisseau Chanion, continuing south to the separate Bujeault junction, and then running southwest and south toward Rivière-Saint-Paul. This broad bend sequence corresponds to the lower selected corridor; tributary names are not extended onto the selected trunk.

subcomponents.part: Lower settlement reach and receiving coast
observations: The original figure continues the lower river through the Rivière-Saint-Paul settlement/coastal-transition setting into the island-fringed coast. The Commission account separately places the named river outlet in Baie des Esquimaux in the Vieux Fort archipelago, with the village on its western side. This supports the ordinary terminal setting without treating the model sea class as proof of a precise open-Gulf mouth.
